title: Quinones's metronome training for tempo
summary: The guitar professor trained students to hold tempo by covering the metronome and playing on.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Dr. Tishner's antiseptic. Well, they could improve. But could you knock it in their head to keep tempo? Dr. Tishner's antiseptic. No. That would be less. That's something that you can't learn a poison. It's got to come from under your heart. Dr. Tishner's antiseptic. In other words, you've got to have that feeling. If you haven't got that feeling, nothing happens. Now, I'll show you what I mean about that. We're coming right back to this old professor, Francisco Quinones. When he was learning us, he had about, let's see, it was Mossoy and King, myself. There was three of us. And I don't forgot the other fellow. There was four of us, I know. But I can't think of the other. Whoever the other poison is. Now, you know what they call a metronome? That is just like your clock. You can't beat it. You understand? Now, what he used to do with us, he used to take this and say, all right, here's the metronome. In Spanish. Uno, dos, tres, cuatro. Uno, dos, tres, cuatro. Uno, dos, tres, cuatro. Uno, dos, tres, cuatro. Now, he said, take it from there. Plum, plum, plum, plum, plum, plum. On the guitar. Turn your face. Away from it. See? And he smothered the microphone. So you couldn't hear it. Couldn't hear it. But keep on playing. Plum, plum, plum, plum, plum, plum, plum. Then he'd take it off. And we're all in. If it was out, if it was too fast or too slow, he says, see? He says, that don't lie. He says, that's what I want you to do. Well, it seems like I don't want to, you know what I mean. I don't want no flowers or nothing like that. But he used to praise me and sometimes he used to call a bunch of friends and show them what I could do. He used to take that mic, three, four tempo, waltz tempo, two, four tempo, any kind of tempos at all and set that mic. See? Like that. I'd go as far as getting the tempo from there, keep on playing and go to the next room and come back and be playing with that thing when he uncovers it. Now that's how strictly I played tablet. That's why he changed his mind. When he seen that I progressed so good, that's why I said before, he wanted me to play piano. But when he played, he wanted me to play piano and he wanted me to start reading music, I quit. That was it.
